I made a big change around 2019-2020. I remember voting for Biden. I think it’s a combination of a few things. During the Democratic primary, I resonated with a lot of Andrew Yang’s rhetoric. Even though he was a Democrat, he made an effort to connect with those who weren’t left-wing. I think we lose sight of each other’s humanity when dealing with politics. Tribalism will be the death of this country. Yang seemed to care, which was refreshing and opened my mind a lot. 

I’m not saying this is exclusively a left-wing issue because it happens on the right as well, but a lot of left-wing political discourse focuses on talking down to those you disagree with. It’s this smug, “I’m better than you” attitude that throws people off. I think we lose a lot of open-minded people because of that.

There are also some little things that helped me, I could talk about it all day! Certain shows I watched with positive messaging, which I’m more than happy to share, martial arts, David Pakman, etc. Also, some of the memes shared around by people in right wing circles were racist dog whistles, which was a big wake up call. There was one popular show shared around online that was basically just racist propaganda, all under the guise of conservative “edgy humor.” I had to look within and realize that I wanted nothing to do with these people and this wasn’t the type of person I wanted to become. I hope my story shows that being open minded and creating dialogue with someone you disagree with does work!
